top_story_title: APT exploits KEV-listed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller auth bypass to plant KeyDrift malware
top_story_summary: An advanced persistent threat group tracked as UAT-11473 is exploiting CVE-2026-20127, the authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart) and Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage), to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift. The flaw exists because the peering authentication mechanism does not work properly; an unauthenticated attacker sends crafted requests and logs in as an internal high-privileged account, then reaches NETCONF and manipulates configuration for the whole SD-WAN fabric.
top_actions: Inventory every Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and SD-WAN Manager instance with its running version; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and patch the controller and manager before touching edge devices.

Remove controller and manager management access from the internet and any untrusted interface; restrict to a dedicated management network with an explicit allowlist, and enforce MFA on the orchestrator.
Work CISA Emergency Directive 26-03 and CISA's Hunt & Hardening Guidance for Cisco SD-WAN Devices as the hunt baseline, not as a patching checklist.

Hunt for KeyDrift and for exploitation: NETCONF sessions and configuration commits from unexpected source addresses, new or unfamiliar local/internal accounts, and template or policy changes with no matching change record.
Assume pre-patch compromise: rotate controller admin credentials, API tokens, certificates and device trust material, and validate certificate trust across the fabric after upgrade.
executive_summary: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller/Manager: KEV-listed auth bypass CVE-2026-20127 is being exploited by a new APT (UAT-11473) to deploy KeyDrift malware. Controller compromise means fabric-wide config control - patch and hunt, do not just patch.

Cisco firewalls: CISA added a Cisco firewall denial-of-service flaw to KEV on evidence of active exploitation, and Cisco has confirmed attackers are crashing its firewalls with a newly disclosed vulnerability. The collected summaries do not name that CVE - read the KEV entry and Cisco's advisory.
Palo Alto Networks rates the impact of the two KEV-listed PHP unauthenticated RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on its products as CRITICAL. KEV remediation was due 2026-10-29.

Cisco's October Node.js advisory carries four high-severity flaws affecting Cisco products, including the KEV-listed Brotli decoder bug CVE-2026-111497 (KEV due 2026-11-10) and two TLS hostname-validation bypasses.
Cisco Finesse SSRF CVE-2026-20362 has no workaround and no released fix - not network infrastructure, but it will land in the same patch queue.
Four of five consequential items this cycle are third-party component flaws (PHP, Node.js, Brotli, Linux kernel) reaching network devices - component CVEs now drive appliance patch cycles.

AI: Cisco open sourced Project Quarry for detecting agent attacks spread across benign steps; Check Point described audio guardrails for voice agents and shipped the Maestro MHO 200 for inspecting AI-scale data center traffic.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Patch orchestrator/controller before edge devices; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and validate certificate trust across the fabric after upgrade.
**Cisco** — Restrict controller and manager access to management networks only, remove any internet exposure, and enforce MFA on the orchestrator.
**Multiple** — Confirm the running version of every internet-facing firewall against the vendor's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first.

**Multiple** — Identify which of your firewalls embed a PHP-based management or captive-portal component and prioritise those; apply the vendor advisory for the PHP flaws and for the Linux kernel bug on any appliance that exposes a patchable OS.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Read advisory CVE-2026-109618 and map the affected product and version list against your inventory before planning anything else - the feed entry carries no product detail.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Confirm running versions against the vendor's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first; check the advisory for the fixed release rather than assuming a build.
**Cisco** — Pull the current KEV catalog entry for the Cisco firewall flaw to get the CVE and affected platform list, then confirm your running versions against Cisco's fixed-release table.
**Cisco** — Schedule the firewall upgrade in the change window, HA pair secondary first, and verify HA failover works before you need it.

headlines.title: Chinese hackers used VMware ESX zero-day; PHP2Shell and Fragnesia chained to root firewalls
headlines.summary: China-nexus actors chained PHP2Shell flaws with the Fragnesia Linux kernel bug to root servers and firewalls, and Cisco confirmed attackers are crashing its firewalls with a new flaw.
